name: #include
description: #include is a passionate group of students at University of California, Davis that builds custom web solutions for local organizations. We serves two main purposes: to support local organizations by delivering high quality custom web solutions to establish their web presence, and to provide a collaborative environment where students of all skill levels can learn the fundamentals of web programming and UI/UX design. We are open to all majors and no prior experience is required. During Fall 2025, #include meets every other Tuesday from 8:00-9:00 PM in Walker 1310, starting on October 21st.

name: 180 Degrees Consulting at UC Davis
description: 180 Degrees Consulting aims to empower nonprofits and social enterprises by providing high-impact, pro bono consulting services delivered by student volunteers. Our mission centers on turning good organizations into great ones through strategic advice and a socially motivated mindset.

name: 27 Heartbeats
description: Our goal is to provide medical care to animals in need by collecting and distributing unused medical supplies, while offering students educational and hands on experiences with animals. We also aim to educate our community about the importance of animal welfare and wildlife conservation around the world. Members are notified about upcoming events / meetings and sign ups through club emails (typically sent out weekly). name: 3 Day Event Club at UC Davis
description: The 3 Day Event Club at UC Davis aims to foster a sense of community amongst collegiate equestrians and support our members in their persual of the eventing sport, regardless of skill or competition level.

name: 3D Enthusiasts of Davis
description: To connect people interested in sharing and learning with each other about 3D modeling, rendering, sculpting, and more and foster creative collaboration with club projects and events. First meeting Fall Quarter October 7th.

description: We believe that addiction awareness for all individuals reduces stigma. We aim to center the voices of our students in everything we do to advocate and ground our work in unity, where all individuals facing addiction do not face isolation and can seek harm reduction resources. We hope to educate peers- growing a community where we can support recovering students and more. We strive to create inclusive, compassionate spaces where education, open dialogue, and peer support are prioritized. name: Advanced Modeling Aeronautics Team
description: Advanced Modeling Aeronautics Team (AMAT) is an organization that teaches undergraduate students the necessary hands-on experience to design, build, and fly scale model remote-controlled (RC) airplanes. AMAT competes in the annual SAE Aero Design / AIAA DBF competition. We build and fly large, remote-controlled aircraft made primarily from composite materials such as carbon fiber, honeycomb aluminum, and foam. name: Adventist Christian Fellowship at UC Davis
description: Adventist Christian Fellowship is a student organization on campus dedicated and passionate about the life and ministry of Jesus Christ. Our purpose on campus is to exemplify the character and love of our Savior through fellowship and friendship.

name: Advocates for Missing & Exploited Children
description: Advocates for Missing & Exploited Children (AMEC) is dedicated to educating families, communities, and local officials by providing accessible prevention resources. Alongside our community outreach efforts, AMEC supports families of missing and exploited children by offering volunteer efforts and civic engagement in finding their loved ones. While our primary efforts are rooted in helping children and adolescents within our immediate communities, we are steadfast advocates for all children and approach every case with equal care and commitment.

name: Afghan Student Association
description: The Afghan Student Association (ASA) intends to promote awareness, tolerance, and peace in issues relating to Afghanistan in UC Davis and the surrounding communities. ASA recognizes that the gateway to achieving the ultimate goal of peace resides in knowledge and understanding. It is for this reason that the ASA's mission includes promoting an understanding of Afghan religion, culture, and politics.

name: African Diaspora Mental Health
description: This club will give additional assistance, empowerment, and opportunity for African Diaspora students to prosper, while also building a more inclusive and equitable campus climate.

name: African Graduate and Professional Students Association
description: Fostering a vibrant community, the African Graduate and Professional Students Association is dedicated to cultivating a forum for networking, collaboration, mentoring, and effective communication between African graduate students and professional students. Our mission is to provide a supportive platform that empowers scholars, encouraging both personal and professional growth while fostering a spirit of unity and shared opportunities.

name: Agape
description: Agape (ah-gah-pay; Greek for conditional love) is a non-audition dance crew at UCD that dances to experience and share the GREAT love and joy of God. Agape, created in 2012, is an all-styles dance group represented and founded on unconditional love. They strive to have fun, inspire others, encourage compassion, and spread this love they learned from Jesus Christ through dance. No auditions, no religious background, and no experience necessary to join. We just want to further the kingdom of God by going all out in dance and being a part of this overflow of love! Contact us at agapeucd@gmail.com

name: Aggie Baking Club
description: Aggie Baking Club welcomes bakers from every kind of background and culture, with any kind of skill level, and those who just love eating the yummy baked goods. We are dedicated to not only having a fun time over some muffins and madeleines, but also introducing bakers to recipes from different cultures and new ways of baking that include every kind of diet. We have meetings where we trade baked goods, watch parties of baking show favorites like the Great British Baking Show, baking parties, and more! Join Our Discord: https://discord.gg/hPKUvDKVBF

name: Aggie Barbell Club at UC Davis
description: At Aggie Barbell, we welcome lifters of all backgrounds and experience levels. Our mission is to create a supportive and inclusive community where every member can pursue their personal fitness goals. We strive to foster an environment of camaraderie and mutual growth through group lifts, gym visits, and social events. Whether you're a seasoned athlete or new to lifting, Aggie Barbell is committed to helping you build strength, confidence, and lasting friendships. Together, we lift each other up.

name: Aggie Bullet Journaling and Productivity Club
description: The Aggie Bullet Journaling and Productivity Club is a community of students at UC Davis who enjoy journaling as an outlet for productivity, organization, mental health and wellness, creativity, and academic success. We host workshops and social events to meet other bullet journalers and anyone else who is interested in learning what bullet journaling is all about. Come learn how you can use a bullet journal as a tool to help you achieve your personal and academic goals! Interested in joining? Visit our website at aggiebujos.carrd.co for the link to join our Discord server.

name: Aggie Fiction Writing Workshop
description: Aggie Fiction Writing Workshop aims to create a constructive literary environment where students feel welcomed and motivated to improve their creative writing. Our weekly workshops are student-run and student-led with a focus on fiction pieces, but all student-produced works are welcome. Students can volunteer to workshop their stories (finished or not) on specific dates and will have part of that week's meeting dedicated to comments and critiques for their piece. In addition, meetings will consist of free-write exercises and other activities designed to stimulate creativity. At Aggie Fiction,

name: Aggie Goth & Alternative Society
description: The Aggie Goth & Alternative Culture Society at UC Davis is a student-led organization dedicated to building an inclusive and expressive community for individuals who identify with or are interested in Goth culture and its related aesthetics, music, fashion, and philosophy. We aim to create a safe and welcoming space for creative expression, critical discussion, and social connection through events, meetups, and collaborations. We celebrate the diversity and depth of alternative identities and promote understanding of the Goth subculture within and beyond the UC Davis community.

name: Aggie House
description: Aggie House is an organization operating a student-run transitional housing shelter for UC Davis students experiencing housing insecurity and homelessness. Data from the ASUCD-GSA Housing Affordability and Insecurity Survey shows that over the course of the 2017-18 school year, 18% of UC Davis students experienced either homelessness or some form of housing insecurity. Our program seeks to address this issue by providing additional emergency shelter options for students, while also taking an innovative approach of being community-based, as well as volunteer and student-led. name: Aggie Hurricane Skating Club
description: The Aggie Skate Club, founded in 2019, exists to celebrate the art of skateboarding at our very own UC Davis Campus. Our mission is to foster connection, creativity, and stoke through skating while growing an inclusive skater community in our community.

name: Aggie International Ministry
description: We are a “home away from home” for international students all over the world. AIM stands for Aggie International Ministry; we are a Christian group at UC Davis. Whether you have beliefs or no beliefs and whether you are an undergrad or graduate student, visiting scholar or post-doc, you are welcome here! We gather together weekly in our homes to eat yummy food, study the Bible together, engage in thought-provoking discussions, and also make time to play fun games. Aside from our weekly gatherings, we also host various educational workshops to help international students adjust to living and st

name: Aggie International Ministry - Undergrad
description: AIM-Undergrad is an International Christian group on campus for undergraduate students. There exists a separate group for graduate students. :) We spend time learning the Bible, getting connected with other international Christian students, and having fun! We seek to build community that is encompassing, unique, and open. We meet regularly and hope to help international students transition to American life. Whether you want to learn about Christianity or looking to connect with other like-minded students, anyone is free to check us out!

name: Aggie Mahjong Club
description: The purpose of the Aggie Mahjong Club is to bring UC Davis students together to learn how to play and enjoy the game of Mahjong. The club will meet up to play recreational games of Mahjong while eating snacks and enjoying other refreshments. Students will learn about the history and culture of mahjong through playing and occasional seminars. Mahjong tournaments will be held each academic year so that students can put the skills they have gained to practical use and have fun!

name: Aggie Neurodiversity Community
description: The Aggie Neurodiversity Community (ANC) is a social community of undergraduate and graduate students, as well as general community members, who identify as neurodivergent. Neurodiversity is broadly and inclusively defined, no diagnoses necessary, so as to create as welcoming and diverse a space as we can. We work side-by-side with the Disabled Student Union, another UC Davis club, to create a space for disability cultures while supporting and empowering our communities. name: Aggie Open Mics
description: The purpose of this organization is to foster a space for students of diverse backgrounds to express themselves creatively and feel heard in various ways of expression, including but not limited to singing, dancing, poetry, and storytelling. Aggie Open Mics aims to allow for collaboration, friendships, and creating a community where we can be ourselves comfortably.

name: Aggie Poetry Club
description: The mission of the Aggie Poetry Club is to foster a community for those passionate about poetry. This club will allow those interested in poetry to connect with others through workshops, readings, and other fun events. Our meetings will be aimed towards promoting creativity, critical thinking, and self expression through the art of poetry and the dialogue surrounding it.

name: Aggie Polo Club at UC Davis
description: The Aggie Polo Club gives students the opportunity to learn the sport of polo along with horsemanship, barn management, and horse care. The club is student operated with the help of alumni volunteers. Practices and lessons will take place off-campus and include scrimmages and interactive clinics.

name: Aggie PreMed Mentorship
description: To facilitate connection between pre-medical undergraduates and UC Davis School of Medicine students for purposes of mentorship. Our mission is to provide information and advice about the process and steps needed in order to become a medical student. We also wish to provide mentors for those pre medical students that want to have a medical student share advice in a one-on-one type environment.

name: Aggie Propulsion & Rocketry Lab
description: Aggie Propulsion & Rocketry Lab (APRL) is a student-run bi-propellant liquid-fueled rocketry team. We are working towards building UC Davis's first-ever liquid rocket. Our project will enable students at Davis to design, build, test, and launch rockets for years to come. Our mission is three-fold. Make rocketry accessible to all students regardless of background or experience. Create a community of like-minded individuals sharing their passion for space and rocketry. name: Aggie Rally Committee
description: The purpose of this organization shall be to organize all rallies and activities of the student section, to act as the official guardian of the traditions and spirit of the University of California Davis, to represent the traditions of fair play, justice, and immense pride for the ideals of the University to the public, the students, and the alumni.

name: Aggie Society of Emergency Medical Technicians
description: The Aggie Society of Emergency Medical Technicians (ASEMT) is dedicated to fostering a scholarly society of current and aspiring emergency medical technicians dedicated to excellence in prehospital care. Our mission is to provide professional development, mentorship, and community service initiatives that equip future EMTs with the leadership, knowledge, and skills necessary to respond confidently in medical emergencies. name: Aggie Space Initiative
description: The Aggie Space Initiative (ASI) empowers UC Davis students to contribute to the future of space exploration through interdisciplinary collaboration, hands-on projects, and student-led innovation. We believe every field has a place in space exploration, and we bring students from all majors together through NASA competitions, research, and technical projects to tackle real challenges in human spaceflight and space systems.

name: Aggie Sports Analytics
description: Aggie Sports Analytics is a student-led organization redefining the future of sports technology. We unite driven students from diverse academic backgrounds to develop innovative solutions across business, technology, and media.

name: Aggie Wrestling Club
description: Our mission is to bring wrestling to UC Davis by building a welcoming and hardworking community for athletes of all skill levels. Whether someone is stepping onto the mat for the first time or continuing years of experience, we strive to create an environment that promotes growth, discipline, competition, and camaraderie through the sport of wrestling.

name: Aggie's Digital Asset Management
description: The objective of ADAM is to create a learning environment where the students of the University of California, Davis can learn and acquire knowledge on investing, stock markets, cryptocurrency, and blockchain technology through participating in study groups, mock trading in stocks and cryptocurrencies, practical sessions, and digital assets project development.

name: Aggiemation Eggheads
description: Aggiemation Eggheads is an animation club where students of all skill levels and backgrounds can learn to animate, collaborate on projects and/or meet new people! Currently, our club operates as a animation studio! We work as a team to create a finished animated film by the end of each academic year! Fall is Pre-Production, Winter Production, and Spring is Post-Production. name: AggieMed Bookworms
description: The mission of AggieMed Bookworms is to provide a place for all book lovers in the School of Medicine to meet and discuss non-medicine-related books and to attend book-related events (e.g., the Sacramento Book Festival, film adaptations) together.

name: Aggies for Israel
description: Aggies For Israel (AFI) is a student organization at UC Davis dedicated to showcasing the diversity and intersectionality of Israeli-Jewish culture. AFI welcomes to any member of the local community who believes in the existence of the Jewish State of Israel, regardless of ethnicity, gender, orientation, affiliation, or religion.

name: Aggies For The Arb (Cleaning Organization)
description: We are committed to preserving and protecting the UC Davis Arboretum, a cherished cornerstone of our campus community, through active stewardship, litter removal, and pollution reduction, ensuring this natural sanctuary remains a thriving, beautiful space for generations of Aggies to come.

name: Aggies Near and Far
description: Our organizational goal is to develop a podcast dedicated to promoting international collaboration, fostering cultural literacy, and highlighting the opportunities available to UC Davis students, faculty, and staff. The podcast aims to spark curiosity and reflections about how global learning shapes personal and academic growth. We interview students, faculty, visiting scholars, and members of the UC Davis community with diverse global backgrounds to amplify the voices and cultural experiences of Aggies. name: AggieWorks
description: AggieWorks is a student-run community of product managers, designers, and engineers, and marketers focused on building software products (web and mobile apps) for the UC Davis student body. We believe in helping the UC Davis community by creating solutions that solve student pain points and make college life easier. We hope that through AggieWorks and our products, we are able to help the student community get quality and reliable resources for education and so much more. description: The AI in Medicine SIG fosters meaningful dialogue and provides practical education around how artificial intelligence is actively reshaping healthcare. At the micro level, we focus on teaching students how to safely and effectively use current AI tools to enhance their daily studying and preclinical workflows. description: The AI Collective is a national network of student organizations dedicated to providing accessible AI & tech literacy through professional development programs and events. name: Alpha Tau Omega
description: Alpha Tau Omega’s mission is “to bind men together in a brotherhood based upon eternal and immutable principles, with a bond as strong as right itself and as lasting as humanity."

description: Alzheimer’s Buddies is a national student organization that responds to the isolation and social disengagement experienced by people in the intermediate to late stages of Alzheimer’s Disease. Through the course of weekly, one-on-one visits, our undergraduate volunteers provide companionship to dementia residents, break down communication barriers, and build bridges between families and their loved ones.

description: Our mission is to empower today's students by fostering a strong network of alumni who provide mentorship, guidance, resources, and opportunities based on our collective love of humanity. We will do both career fairs with companies we have made connections with and mentorship programs between current students and Davis alumni who have made it in the students desired fields.

description: Benefit environmental engineering and environmental science undergraduate students and related engineering and scientific disciplines; provide community, information, resources, and support to environmental engineering and science undergraduate students. description: American Cancer Society at UC Davis, formerly known as Colleges Against Cancer, is designed to help eliminate cancer by initiating and supporting the programs of the American Cancer Society on the college campus. name: American Indian Health Alliance
description: AIHA is dedicated to supporting Indigenous students in their journey into the health professions. Along with support for health professions, AIHA aims to support the Indigenous student community's overall wellness physically, spiritually, and socially.

description: The mission of the American Indian Science and Engineering Society (AISES) is to substantially increase the representation of American Indians and Alaskan Natives in engineering, science, and other related technology disciplines. description: We are the official student chapter of the American Institute of Aeronautics and Astronautics (AIAA) at the University of California (UC), Davis. name: American Institute of Architects for Students at UC Davis
description: The American Institute of Architects for Students (AIAS) strives for advancing leadership, design, and service among architecture students. Our vision for prospective architects includes a more sustainable, healthy, and equitable future through the empowerment of student voices, ideas, and actions. At UC Davis, the AIAS is meant to provide resources, career opportunity, and academic excellence in the architectural field.

description: The American Institute of Chemical Engineers (AIChE) is the world’s leading organization for chemical engineering professionals, with more than 40,000 members from 93 countries. description: The mission of the American Lung Cancer Screening Initiative is to promote lung cancer screening for people who are at high risk of developing lung cancer.

description: AMWA at UC Davis SOM is a local branch of a national organization whose goal is to advance women in medicine and improve women's health. description: The Muslim Medical Student Association (MMSA) aims to cultivate a vibrant collective environment and a strong sense of community that extends beyond our Muslim students to embrace all peers and colleagues. To foster understanding and collaboration among diverse backgrounds, we envision hosting innovative projects and inclusive sessions, such as interfaith dialogue workshops, health education outreach initiatives, and cultural competency training. name: American Red Cross Club at UC Davis
description: Guided by the mission of the American Red Cross, our mission is to prevent and alleviate human suffering in the face of emergencies by mobilizing the power of volunteers and the generosity of donors. The American Red Cross Club at UC Davis will learn, practice and exemplify humanitarian values through service projects upholding the Red Cross mission.

description: American Society of Microbiology (ASM) is a club dedicated to creating a community for students interested in microbiology at UC Davis. Our goal is to make research information and internship opportunities surrounding microbiology more accessible to students while forming networking connections with faculty and staff. Members of ASM get hands-on experience with academia, from assisting in labs to attending conferences to taking trips out into the field. Feel free to contact us for more information on Aggie Life! description: The American Society of Civil Engineers at the University of California, Davis strives to promote the professional success of future civil engineers. description: American Society of Mechanical Engineers (ASME) at UC Davis is dedicated to building a community of aspiring mechanical engineers. We strive to improve the quality of life through innovation, collaboration, and a passion for engineering, while inspiring others with the excitement of our field.

description: We are a student chapter of the American Water Works Association and aim to provide students of UC Davis with access to connections and professional development within the water industry. description: The goal of the interest group is to promote exploration of the broad specialty of anesthesiology. The SIG will host informational talks from faculty mentors, organize procedure workshops, and facilitate shadowing of anesthesiologists. Given the minimal exposure to peri-operative and pain medicine during third year clerkships at UC Davis, the interest group is an essential component of our school's commitment to training leaders in all areas of medicine.

We believe in providing the utmost care for animals, while working to ensure a healthy, wholesome and safe food supply to benefit the world. We have the unique responsibility to bring sound scientific evidence to our future clients and to educate the consuming public about the food they eat. This mission begins in school and continues throughout our careers as food animal practitioners.

name: Fellowship of Coptic Christian University Students
description: We are a Coptic club with hopes of engaging the community through weekly bible studies.

Group members share academic success strategies, socialize, network, and engage in on and off campus activities.

description: King Hall’s First Generation Advocates program was created to promote diversity and maximize the academic, professional, and personal success of students who are the first from their families to earn a college or professional degree, as well as students from low-income backgrounds.

Our goal is to support scholars who are the first in their families to navigate higher education and provide the tools for personal, academic, and professional success.

name: First-Year Aggie Connections

Working with the Sacramento and Yolo County Departments of Public Health, as well as UC Davis attending physicians, we train vaccinators, provide information about the benefits of the flu shot, outreach to our local community, and administer vaccines.

description: "Food for Thought" is committed to promoting awareness and understanding of the integral role of nutrition and exercise in medicine and healthcare. Our ultimate goal is to compile these recipes into an online recipe book, fostering a global community united by a passion for nutritious eating. description: H2O is an open-style performance dance crew at UC Davis that specializes in Hip Hop/Contemporary fusion. The acronym 'H2O' is short for Home To One. We believe dance is a universal language that brings people from all backgrounds together. Our values lie in celebrating what makes each individual mover unique, while fostering a sense of unity among our dancer community.

name: HackDavis
description: Our purpose is to build and facilitate a culture of creating and pursuing diverse social good projects outside the classroom, unlock the innovative spirit of students, and connect builders across different interests. We host UC Davis' annual collegiate hackathon and hold technical workshops throughout Fall Quarter to prepare students of all majors for both this event and their future goals. We usually recruit new Directors a few weeks after our flagship hackathon. Keep an eye out on our social media for updates about this if you're interested in joining the HackDavis Team!

name: HaiLuo Mental Support

name: Hands on the Land
description: Hands on the Land seeks to cultivate a mindset of place-based renewal among people at UC Davis and beyond. We believe working hands and minds can nurture a thriving ecosystem. Our goal is to cultivate a mindset of place-based renewal through hands-on learning. We expect our members to give what they can, whether it be physical labor, intellect, or a novel perspective on our surroundings. Our work addresses large scale issues, such as climate change, through small, local solutions. Through community engagement and creative land management, we hope to restore functional landscapes together.

name: Harm Reduction and Addiction Medicine SIG
description: The HRAM SIG brings together students who are interested in pursuing addiction medicine and/or who aim to incorporate the closely related tenants of harm reduction into their future practice as physicians. We strive to educate our peers and local communities about addiction medicine and harm reduction topics to better the health of people who experience addiction or use drugs.

name: Hear Your Song @ UCD
description: Hear Your Song at UC Davis is a chapter of the national nonprofit Hear Your Song, Inc., which empowers children and teens with serious illnesses and complex health needs to express themselves through original songwriting. Our chapter works directly with these young individuals to write lyrics, compose and produce their songs, and create music videos—all through a collaborative, kid-driven process. Volunteers have the opportunity to work one-on-one with children remotely, helping bring each child’s creative vision to life while centering their voice, imagination, and individuality.

name: Hiking & Camping Student Interest Group

With this in mind, NeuroLOVE aspires to build an empathetic and informed generation of healthcare workers across America.

Our goal is to deepen understanding of neurosurgical practice, cutting-edge research, and the realities of training and life as a neurosurgeon.

description: Neurotech@Davis is a community at the undergraduate level here at UC Davis focused on the field of neuortechnology. name: Nigerian Student Association
description: The Nigerian Students Association (NSA) is a student organization that serves to bring Nigerian students together to form a unified community, to create the awareness of Nigerian culture on the UC Davis campus and beyond. It also aims to form a community that provides a network for students, educate students about Nigerian culture, inform them of political news, and the beautiful heritage of Nigeria, to encourage students to contribute to the prosperity of Nigeria. description: This club is a place for fans of any and every Nintendo (or Nintendo-related) game or franchise to gather, talk, and play Nintendo games together. We strive to build a welcoming community, and create a space in which people can find a break from their busy schedules. There is no structure of membership, meaning that EVERYONE is welcome at all times. description: Nishkam Sewa was founded with the Sikh tenant of Sewa (selfless service) in mind. description: Noor Community Health exists to provide accessible, culturally competent primary and preventive care to the underserved communities of Woodland, CA, primarily first-generation, low-income Pakistani residents. description: The UC Davis North African Student Society is dedicated to celebrating and promoting the diverse cultures, histories, and identities of North Africa, including Morocco, Algeria, Tunisia, Libya, Egypt, Sudan, and Mauritania. Through social events, cultural showcases, discussions, and collaborations, we aim to foster a strong sense of community among North African students by sharing our traditions and perspectives with the broader UC Davis campus. description: We are Nursing club at UC Davis and this club serves to educate those who are interested in pursuing nursing careers beyond their UC Davis education. name: Nutritional Biology Graduate Student Advisory Committee
description: The GGNB GradSAC is a student-run group comprised of Graduate Group in Nutritional Biology students and one faculty advisor. name: oSTEM at UC Davis
description: Out in Science, Technology, Engineering, and Mathematics (oSTEM), Inc. is a non-profit professional society focused on LGBTQ people in the STEM community. description: The Pakistani Student Association at the University of California, Davis aims to provide a supportive and welcoming community for both Pakistani students and those interested in Pakistani culture on campus through general body meetings, quarterly events, our annual cultural banquet, and much more. description: The Pediatrics SIG is committed to bringing in speakers, promoting shadowing opportunities, and organizing events with children in the community to expose medical students to the field of Pediatrics and to learn more about the field as a career path.

description: P.E.A.C.E. description: Phi Alpha Delta is the world’s preeminent law fraternity because of our dedication to service: service to the student, the school, the profession, and the community. Through accepting our differences we become not just a law fraternity, but a family.

Whether you're preparing for Wall Street, real estate, venture capital, or professional development in your career, PGN provides the tools to launch your career.

description: The Phi Sigma Biological Sciences Honor Society was founded in 1915 at Ohio State University. The Gamma Delta Chapter was established at UC Davis in 1984 by a group of students and faculty members who wanted to provide recognition to outstanding undergraduate students. Among the founders are Dr. Barbara Horwitz, past vice president, and Dr. John Horowitz, past treasurer.

name: Philosophical GeMS (Gender Minoritized Students)
description: Philosophical Gender Minoritized Students (GeMS) is a social club for philosophically minded undergraduates identifying as women, nonbinary, transgender, or other identities outside of the gender binary. description: The Physics Club at UC Davis brings together students who share an interest in physics. General meetings are Fridays at 5 PM in Physics 185. You can also visit us in Physics 388, the Physics Club Room.

We also hold a monthly journal club to provide educational opportunity where students can meet and promote knowledge in plant breeding together.

description: Plant Futures is a network of students, academics, and professionals that is broadly focused on accelerating the transition to plant-based food systems at the intersection of social justice, public health, and environmental sustainability. name: Preventive Medicine SIG

description: The UC Davis Table Tennis Club provides students with opportunities to learn, practice, compete, and connect through the sport of table tennis. description: We, the members of the TSA( Taiwanese Student Association) at UC Davis, gather together for our common interests in Taiwanese culture. We provide amazing Taiwanese cuisine and snacks at many of our events. Do not hesitate to ask us any questions. name: Urology Student Interest Group
description: The goal of the Urology SIG is to provide medical students the opportunity to learn about and explore careers in the field of urology. Urology is a surgical subspecialty that students are often exposed to during their third year surgical rotation, however this if often too late to build an competitive application for the early urology match without taking a research year. Further, many students are never exposed to the field of urology at all. The UroSIG hopes to bridge this gap in career opportunity exposure.

name: UV&ME at UC DAVIS
description: Sun Safety for Kids, a nonprofit founded in 2001 by board-certified dermatologists from the Los Angeles Metropolitan Dermatological Society, aims to combat the preventable epidemic of skin cancer by promoting sun protection among youth. In 2016, medical students from the Keck School of Medicine of USC: Vadim Lincoln, Igor Krivitsky, and Shera Feinstein—developed a skin cancer prevention presentation that led to a partnership with Sun Safety for Kids. name: Vascular Surgery Interest Group
description: Our vision with the UC Davis Vascular Surgery Interest Group is to create opportunities for medical students at UC Davis to gain exposure to vascular surgery well before starting their clinical clerkships. We aim to assist students create a competitive application for residency by providing our members opportunities to get involved in leadership, research, and scholarly publication. Through mentorship, members will connect with vascular surgeons, fellows, and residents. name: Vet Aide Club
description: By joining the Vet Aide Club, you can learn more about opportunities to gain practical, hands-on experience in a variety of animal care fields. Our members run the gamut of animal disciplines, including Animal Science, Avian Science, and Wildlife, Fish and Conservation Biology, to name a few. Our VAC members learn invaluable information about a wide variety of careers in animal care and the steps you need to take to get there. name: Veterinarians as One Inclusive Community for Empowerment
description: VOICE (Veterinarians as One Inclusive Community for Empowerment) is a student run organization that addresses the need for diversity and inclusion in the field of veterinary medicine at UC Davis. The purpose of VOICE is to celebrate all facets of diversity within the profession of veterinary medicine and provide a campus environment that embraces such values and promotes the success of students, particularly underrepresented students. name: Veterinary Business Management Association at UC Davis School of Veterinary Medicine
description: VBMA strives to supplement the veterinary student's education with practical information about veterinary business. This includes aspects of ownership, finances, and leadership as it applies specifically to veterinary medicine.

name: Veterinary Medicine Office of Veterinary Success.
description: The Office of Veterinary Success (OVS) within the School of Veterinary Medicine offers numerous career services an resources, including VetMedJobs (an online job board specifically for DVM students). OVS also helps students build, strengthen and assess their leadership skills to foster the highest level of personal and professional development. In addition, the UC Davis School of Veterinary Medicine greatly values the mental health and wellness of its DVM students and as such offers counseling and a host of activities focused on well-being.

name: Veterinary Medicine Surgery Club
description: The Veterinary Medicine Surgery Club at UC Davis is an organization run by veterinary students. The club officers are dedicated to promoting the education of veterinary students in the field of surgery. We host lectures pertaining to the knowledge of surgical procedures and techniques, and we also provide information about externship and internship opportunities. name: Veterinary Pathology Club at UC Davis
description: A club that introduces students to careers in veterinary pathology and further develops pathology-related skills, such as performing a necropsy and participating in slide reading labs. Note: this club is primarily for current veterinary students at UCDSVM

name: Veterinary Radiology Club
description: Diagnostic imaging plays a significant role in Veterinary Medicine. Proper image interpretation requires students to hone pattern recognition skills. The goal of the Radiology Club is to provide students with additional opportunities to discuss clinical cases and perform scans with veterinary radiologists, residents and technicians. By seeing a larger range of normal and abnormal radiographs and ultrasounds, students will acquire the skills necessary to confidently and accurately interpret diagnostic images.

name: Vietnamese Medical Student Association
description: The Vietnamese Medical Student Association (VMSA) fosters a supportive and inclusive community for Vietnamese and allied medical students, grounded in cultural connection, mentorship, and professional development. We are committed to serving Vietnamese and underserved communities by promoting culturally responsive care, expanding access to health education, and engaging in meaningful community outreach. name: Vietnamese Student Association
description: The Vietnamese Student Association at UC Davis - also known as “VSA at UCD”, is a social-cultural student organization at UC Davis that promote a social, supportive, and philanthropic platform that enables the growth of Vietnamese culture, community, and compassion. We accept everyone and anyone into our community regardless of gender, ethnicity, sexual orientation, and capabilities. As long as you are willing to learn and embrace the Vietnamese heritage, you are more than welcome to call VSA at UCD your home. Throughout the year, VSA at UCD hosts events and programs that further uplift our me

name: Vintage Club at UC Davis
description: The UC Davis Vintage Club exists to open a door that has largely gone unopened on this campus. Vintage and secondhand clothing represents one of the most accessible, creative, and sustainable ways to engage with fashion — yet the knowledge behind it remains untapped in our community. Our mission is to make that knowledge available to everyone. We believe that understanding vintage — how to find it, evaluate it, style it, and appreciate its history — is a skill with real value, both personally and professionally. Whether you're a first-time thrifter or someone with a passion for textile history

description: VDT is a jazz and contemporary focused dance group. We perform a couple times throughout the year, including our very own spring showcase! We strive to foster creativity, where everyone has the opportunity to expand their skills in choreographing and dancing. name: Visiting Scholars Ministry
description: The mission for this graduate student group is to welcome and serve all international visiting scholars and post-docs. We strive to provide enriching experiences during their stay in America by introducing them to American culture, life, and Christian faith.

name: Vital Signs at UC Davis
description: Vital Signs is built on a simple but powerful belief: preventive health should be an accessible conversation, not a daunting confrontation. Student life is busy, and routine health checks are often the first thing to be forgotten, leaving basic questions about our bodies unanswered. We are here to change that. Our mission is to demystify basic healthcare and build a healthier, more informed campus community from the ground up. description: VN CARES at the Davis School of Medicine works with the Sacramento Vietnamese community to implement 3 goals: 1. Inform the community about the prevalent types of cancer that affect the target population – namely breast, cervical, and prostate cancer. 2. Educate the community about the benefits of performing regular cancer screenings and the available cancer treatments. 3. Enroll individuals to receive free cancer screenings. name: Volleyball SIG
description: Connect students who want to play volleyball and provide increased opportunities for our UC Davis Health community to access a fun and competitive way to stay active.

name: Walk with a Doc SIG
description: The Walk with a Doc SIG's goal is to establish a chapter of the national organization Walk with a Doc at UC Davis to promote healthy communities and increased communication between doctors and the community.

name: Walking SIG
description: Foster community, wellness, and safety by creating a welcoming environment where students can connect, relieve stress, and prioritize their mental and physical well-being through regular evening walks.

name: Water Association of Law and Policy
description: The Water Association of Law and Policy strives to provide a forum and community for students who seek information on water law practice, to foster utilization of the unique resources at King Hall, to help students accomplish their career goals, and to provide opportunities to network with students and practitioners in the water law and policy field.

name: Wheely Happy Aggies Club
description: Our mission is to provide a safe and fun learning environment for those that want to learn how to rollerskate/rollerblade, as well as a way for people to connect and make new friends.

name: White Coat Collective
description: The White Coat Collective is a digital hub club, uniting hundreds of pre-med and pre-PA students at UC Davis on a single discord server. Our club aggregates pre-health resources around the UC Davis Campus in an open-access format. We share events and opportunities by partnering with organizations, clubs, student run clinics, labs, and programs on one server. We prioritize fostering teamwork, innovation and soft skills in medicine to help pre-health students reach their full potential.

name: Wilderness Medicine Student Interest Group
description: The Wilderness Medicine SIG at UC Davis School of Medicine aims to bring education about providing medical care in austere environments through experiential learning. Our goal is to get students out into nature so they can learn how to give patients high quality care with limited resources. Through a combination of camping trips, speakers, and workshops, we hope to make wilderness medicine a fun and engaging topic for all!

name: Wildlife & Exotic Animal Medicine Club
description: To educate and provide opportunities to undergraduate students with an interest in pursuing wildlife or exotic veterinary medicine

name: Wildlife and Aquatic Animal Medicine
description: A UC Davis Veterinary Medicine Club, for vet students who are interested in pursuing a career in, or are interested in wildlife/zoo/aquatic animal medicine. The Club brings in speakers to educate students on different topics of zoo/wildlife medicine. WAAM holds wetlabs and field-trips for students to gain hands-on experience in various aspect of zoo and wildlife medicine. WAAM also connects students to different zoos and organizations with the goal of furthering student members' careers in wildlife and zoo medicine.

name: Wildlife Photography Club
description: To provide students, both familiar and unfamiliar with wildlife photography, the opportunity to collaborate and share with each other their love for nature! We seek to introduce students to local wildlife, help them identify local flora and fauna, and allow students to contribute to scientific research via iNaturalist.

name: Willow Clinic
description: *This is the undergraduate volunteer group page* The mission of the Willow Clinic is to holistically improve the health of community members who are currently living outside or experiencing homelessness while providing a unique platform for student education. We strive to address inequities in healthcare access by operating a free clinic each Saturday. Community members regardless of documentation, or insurance status, can seek medical and psychiatric care as well as a host of other services. description: The mission of the Willow Clinic is to comprehensively improve the health of the homeless population of Sacramento, while providing a unique platform for undergraduate and professional student education. The Willow Clinic seeks to achieve this by empowering students to operate a makeshift clinic each Saturday, where local homeless individuals can seek medical/psychiatric care as well as a host of other services. name: Wing Chun Kung Fu Club
description: Wing Chun Kung Fu is a Chinese martial art system for self-defense. It emphasizes relaxation, sensitivity, structure, and speed rather than force and strength. The goal of the club is to provide a safe and welcoming place for all to practice Wing Chun Kung Fu.

name: Women and Gender Minorities in Physics
description: Women and Gender Minorities in Physics, WiP+, aims to create a supportive and encouraging space for Women and other Gender Minorities within physics. Our aim is to develop the skills of our members for a successful academic/professional career in or outside of UC Davis.

name: Women In Law
description: Our mission is to empower and support women pursuing careers in law by providing mentorship, professional development, and opportunities to navigate and succeed in the legal field. The Women In Law club at UC Davis strives to prepare students for law school through events and activities that invite professionals from a range of disciplines and backgrounds. Exposure to women who have advanced in their careers will not only help students achieve similar goals, but also demonstrate that those paths are attainable for all. name: Women in Medicine
description: A network of undergraduate students passionate about promoting gender equity in healthcare and dismantling barriers women in medicine face through advocacy, education, leadership, and service.

name: Women in Research at UCD
description: Women in Research at UCD seeks to bridge the gender gap in academia and research. By focusing on three core pillars - supporting women-led research, fostering professional development for women researchers, and promoting impactful research on women. We strive to create an equitable environment for scholarly excellence.

name: Women in STEM at UC DAVIS
description: Our mission is to promote equal opportunities for Women in STEM by fostering mentorship, professional development, networking, and inclusive community engagement. We aim to support academic and career growth, encourage learning and collaboration, and create a welcoming environment where women in STEM can thrive. Through partnerships with organizations such as the Association for Women in Science (AWIS) Sacramento Valley Chapter, we seek to empower and connect the next generation of STEM leaders. We are open to all who share our commitment to supporting and advancing women in STEM.

name: Women Machinists' Club at UC Davis
description: The Women Machinists' Club (WMC) is dedicated to making hands-on learning more accessible and inclusive. Machining, the process of creating parts or products using machines, gives students a way to apply their academic knowledge to practical problems. It builds confidence, critical thinking, and hands-on skills. However, machine shops are often male-dominated spaces, and students of underrepresented genders report experiencing discrimination in these environments. name: Women of Aeronautics & Astronautics at UC Davis
description: Provide support, empowerment, and networking opportunities for gender minorities and underrepresented individuals in the aerospace field.

name: Women of Color Collective
description: The Women of Color Collective (WOCC) is dedicated to creating a safe and empowering community for women of color at UC Davis School of Law (King Hall). We empower our members by fostering a close-knit community in a historically exclusionary and patriarchal field and institution. We create spaces where students identifying as women of color can build community and discuss personal, academic, professional, and social issues in the legal field. name: Women's Initiative for Support and Empowerment
description: The Women’s Initiative for Support and Empowerment (WISE) is a student-led initiative at UC Davis dedicated to supporting women and underserved communities through healthcare advocacy, community service, and education. Our work places particular emphasis on the needs of Middle Eastern, North African, Afghan, refugee, and immigrant communities. From women facing crises abroad to families building new lives in Sacramento and Yolo County, we aim to address barriers such as language differences, cultural disconnects, and limited access to resources. name: Women's Resources and Research Center
description: The Women’s Resources and Research Center (WRRC) challenges all forms of oppression, through the lens of gender equity. The center provides education, advocacy, resources and a safe space that centers the experiences of womxn, transgender, femme and non-binary individuals. The programs and services offered by the center are available to all students.

name: Women's Transportation Seminar (WTS) Student Chapter
description: The WTS @ UC Davis mission is to build the future of transportation and close the gender workforce gap in the global transportation industry by promoting lifelong careers in transportation for women, starting with students. Our primary goal is to expand opportunities for women in the transportation industry (a historically male-dominated field) through the professional development, mentoring, and strategic positioning of women. name: Workers' Rights Clinic at UC Davis
description: The Workers' Rights Clinic is a weekly clinic where law students provide low-income workers with legal information and referrals about problems they are facing at work. The clinic is a student-run organization with law student directors (Principal Officers) and law student counselors (volunteers) willing to spend an evening a week meeting with clients and helping them with their work related issues. name: Yemeni Student Association
description: The role of the YSA (Yemeni Student Association) is to create a community for Yemeni students as well as anyone interested in the culture. Yemeni students are a very small group of students and are often hard to find. This organization will allow them to come together and create a safe space where they can share their culture within themselves as well as others.

name: Young Cattlemens Association
description: YCA at UC Davis strives to create a welcoming environment for all students, regardless of experience or major. We value creating equal opportunities for members with the goal of educating those interested in livestock and strengthening the future of agriculture. Our goal is to provide all students interested in livestock the opportunity to gain hands-on experiences, network with industry leaders, and build community. name: Young Democratic Socialists of America at the University of California, Davis
description: Young Democratic Socialists of America is the youth and student section of the Democratic Socialists of America, and a national organization of recognized campus chapters and several hundred activists. We are students organizing in our universities, colleges, and high schools to fight for the immediate needs of workers and students while building our capacity to fight for more radical and structural changes.

name: Your Mandarin Bridge at UC Davis
description: Create a Chinese-speaking environment where anyone can start to learn or improve their Chinese proficiency. As someone who started learning Chinese a year and a half ago, I understand how hard the basics can be, even with the help of a teacher. My goal for this club is to create an immersive and judgment-free environment so that everyone has more opportunities to speak Chinese. This club will be able to assist those who are unable to take Chinese classes due to schedule conflicts or any other reason. name: Youth In Dentistry at UC Davis
description: Youth in Dentistry at UC Davis is a chapter of the Youth in Dentistry Student Organization. The main purpose of our chapter is to help educate students, regardless of whether they are in high school or college, about the field of dentistry. Along with this, we want to establish this chapter to create a strong sense of community within all the Pre-Dental students at UC Davis itself. We have noticed that there are large communities for Pre-Med, Pre-PA, and Pre-Vet programs but not so much for Pre-Dental students. name: Yoyo Club at UC Davis
description: Yoyo Club at UC Davis is dedicated to introducing students to the fun, creativity, and skill of yoyoing. We hope to build a welcoming community where beginners and experienced players alike can learn, practice, and share their passion for yoyos. Through demonstrations and collaborative practice sessions, we aim to make yoying exciting for all students.

name: Zero Waste and Sustainability Club
description: Zero Waste and Sustainability Club will help the UC Davis campus reach its zero-waste initiatives. Not only will this club focus on campus sustainability, but it will also aim to make our individual lives more sustainable on and off campus, and aim to change the unsustainable habits of the world outside of the UC Davis Campus. The club will involve students in many hands on zero-waste campus projects that reduce and eliminate the campus waste from going into landfills, and other environmentally sustainable projects.
